{{Quote|What is the Voice of the Emperor?''"<br />"''The Voice is the conduit for the Emperor's words.|Servant One explains the Emperor's Voice to the newly appointed Emperor's Wrath|<ref name="The Voice of Darkness" />}}
The '''Emperor's Voice''', formally addressed as the '''Voice of the Emperor''' by other [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] and also known as the '''Voice of Darkness''', was a position within the [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|reconstituted Sith Empire]] that was held by the [[Tenebrae|Sith Emperor's]] host body. First created after a [[Attack on the Sith Emperor|failed assassination attempt]] in [[3950 BBY]], the Voice allowed the [[Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] to protect his true form as a Force entity while still delivering commands to his servants and carrying out his will. The Emperor utilized many Voices of different [[Species/Legends|species]], [[Gender/Legends|genders]], and ages throughout his lifetime, [[Essence transfer|transferring]] his consciousness and [[Force power/Legends|powers]] from body to body as his hosts succumbed to the ravaging effects of the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side]].

As the [[Galactic War]] ignited between the Empire and the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] in [[3642 BBY]], the [[Dark Council]]or [[Darth Baras]] began a [[Darth Baras's coup|coup]] [[Standard year/Legends|years]] in the making as he attempted to take the place of the Voice and thereby become the supreme authority within the Empire. Trapping the true Voice on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Voss]] with the aid of the dark entity [[Sel-Makor]], Baras secured his [[Sphere of Military Offense|power base]] and proclaimed himself to be the Voice of the Emperor before the Dark Council. However, Baras' [[Empire's Wrath|former apprentice]] and the newly-appointed [[Emperor's Wrath]] [[Death/Legends|killed]] the true Voice in order to free the Emperor's [[Living Force/Legends|essence]] and struck down Baras for his transgression. 

The Emperor's next Voice would fall in [[Dromund Kaas operation|battle]] with the prodigal [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] known as the [[Hero of Tython]], forcing the Emperor's essence into hiding and abolishing the post of Emperor's Voice while his essence healed. While not a true Voice in terms of its place in the Sith Empire, the body of the [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Valkorion]] had served as the Emperor's second host body for [[Standard century/Legends|centuries]], ruling over the [[Eternal Empire]] of the planet [[Zakuul]] even as he controlled the Sith Empire through his Voice. Even so, the Emperor was later [[Mission to Kira Carsen's ship|destroyed]] by [[Alliance Commander|the Commander]] of the [[Eternal Alliance]].

==Role and powers==
{{Quote|The Emperor chooses one being to physically embody. This being is the Voice. It is obeyed as the Emperor himself.|Servant One|<ref name="The Voice of Darkness" />}}
Also known as the 'Voice of Darkness,<ref name="The Voice of Darkness" /> the position of Emperor's Voice was more than a simple title&mdash;through [[Sith sorcery/Legends|Sith magic]] and the long-lost technique of [[essence transfer]], the [[Tenebrae|Sith Emperor]] transferred his consciousness and [[Living Force/Legends|life force]] into a host body,<ref name="The Voice of the Emperor">{{TORcite|type=codex|The Voice of the Emperor (Warrior)}}</ref> allowing him to interact with the world as more than just his true state as a being of pure [[The Force/Legends|Force]] energy.<ref name="The End of It All">{{TORcite|exp=shadow|type=general|The End of It All|Ziost}}</ref> The host's mind was completely suppressed, crushed beneath the weight of the [[Emperor/Legends|Emperor's]] mind, and their body literally became the [[Sith/Legends|Sith's]] own. The process also conferred the Emperor's immense [[Force-sensitive/Legends|strength]] in the Force upon the Voice,<ref name="The Voice of the Emperor" /> though his abilities could be bolstered by the host's own powers&mdash;the Emperor utilized a [[Unidentified Emperor's Voice (Voss)|Voss Mystic]] as his Voice during the [[Cold War (Galactic Republic–Sith Empire)|Cold War]] in order to take advantage of the [[Voss (species)|Voss']] prophetic abilities.<ref name="Request An Audience">{{TORcite|type=class|Sith Warrior|Request An Audience|Voss}}</ref>

[[File:Emperor_Valkorion.jpg|thumb|left|220px|Through Valkorion the Emperor ruled the Eternal Empire of Zakuul.]]
When the host Voice died,<ref name="Request An Audience" /> the Emperor's essence was released from the body and returned to the care of his [[Hand of the Empire|Hand]]&mdash;the twelve [[Servant]]s who carried out their master's will across the galaxy. [[Servant Two]], a member of the Emperor's Hand, was mentally linked to the Emperor more so than all of his other agents, and as a result, the prophetic Servant was always aware of the Voice's presence and location even when the Emperor was dormant. Upon receiving their master's essence, the Hand would procure a new Voice for the Emperor and aid him in establishing control of the host body.<ref name="Request An Audience" /> Unbeknownst to all but the Hand, Vitiate&mdash;as the Sith Emperor was once again known as after splitting with the Sith Empire near the end of his life&mdash;also had a second host body that he controlled simultaneously with the Voice: the [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Valkorion]], whose form he used to rule the [[Eternal Empire]] of the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Zakuul]]<ref name="Valkorion">{{TORcite|exp=kotfe|type=codex|Valkorion}}</ref> for [[Standard century/Legends|centuries]].<ref name="Throne">{{TORcite|exp=kotfe|type=codex|The Eternal Throne}}</ref>

==History==
===A new empire===
{{Quote|Wrath. Come to me. I am your Emperor.|The Emperor's Voice encounters his newest Wrath|<ref name="The Voice of Darkness" />}}
[[File:Voice_of_the_Emperor.png|thumb|right|270px|The Voice leaves its host.]]
The Emperor created his first Voice around [[3950 BBY]],<ref name="Encyclopedia" /> after a [[Attack on the Sith Emperor|failed attack]] by the [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Revan/Legends|Revan]] and his allies brought the Emperor's body within arms' reach of harm.<ref name="Revan">''[[The Old Republic: Revan]]''</ref> The Emperor took Revan captive and imprisoned him, but the Emperor&mdash;who feared only [[Death/Legends|death]]&mdash;was terrified by the close brush with death. As a result, the [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|Empire's]] supreme ruler delved into further studies of the dark side in order to preserve his physical form<ref name="Encyclopedia" />&mdash;a body that had been rendered ageless but not invulnerable by the [[Ritual of Nathema|dark]] [[Sith Emperor's ritual|ritual]] the Emperor had performed over a thousand years earlier.<ref name="Revan" /> Discovering how to transfer his consciousness and powers into the bodies of others, he took his first host and named the individual the Voice of the Emperor<ref name="Encyclopedia" />&mdash;the literal embodiment of the Emperor's absolute will and his mouthpiece to the [[Dark Council]].<ref name="The Voice of the Emperor" />

The Dark Council soon learned that the various individuals who would appear throughout the next three centuries were in fact the Emperor's host bodies, and therefore obeyed the Voice's commands the same as they would the Emperor himself.<ref name="The Voice of the Emperor" /> Serving as the focal point of the Emperor's energies, the Voice allowed his consciousness to reach out across the galaxy to direct his agents and observe his enemies. Among the beings that the Emperor used were a [[Unidentified Emperor's Voice (Human female)|young female Human]] and an [[Unidentified Emperor's Voice (Sith Pureblood)|elderly Sith pureblood]],<ref name="The Voice of the Emperor" /> and during the early years of the [[Great Galactic War]] with the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], the position of Voice was filled by a [[Unidentified Human Emperor's Voice (3678 BBY)|male Human]].<ref name="Blood of the Empire 1">''[[The Old Republic, Blood of the Empire Act 1: Shades of the Sith]]''</ref> The Dark Council and the rest of the Sith Empire were unaware, however, that the Voice was not the only host of their ruler&mdash;growing tired of the galaxy and the Sith teachings that limited him, the Emperor established a new kingdom&mdash;an Eternal Empire based on the planet Zakuul in [[Wild Space/Legends|Wild Space]]&mdash;and ruled over it through a host body named Valkorion.<ref name="Valkorion" /> Unlike the Voices, the Emperor ensured that the Valkorion body survived for centuries,<ref name="Throne" /> sparing it the ravaging effects of the dark side. The Emperor split his consciousness and focus between the two Empires, but gradually abandoned the Sith Empire as time went on and invested more of his attentions to Zakuul.<ref name="Valkorion" />

===Plans for immortality===
Around [[3645 BBY]],<ref name="Voss-Date">{{TORcite|type=class|Imperial Agent|Paying Respects|Voss}} establishes that the [[Bas-Ton (imposter)|imposter Bas-Ton]] has been on [[Voss]] for five years, and he was sent there to infiltrate [[Voss (species)|Voss]] society after the [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|Sith Empire's]] invasion of the planet failed. Additionally, ''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic Encyclopedia]]'' places the events of Act III, which include Voss, in approximately [[3640 BBY]]; thus, the invasion of Voss occurred in approximately [[3645 BBY]]. Finally, {{TORcite|type=class|Sith Warrior|Request An Audience|Voss}} establishes that the [[Unidentified Emperor's Voice (Voss)|Voss host]] for the Emperor was taken simultaneously with the [[Imperial Attack on Voss|planet's discovery]].</ref> the planet [[Voss]] was discovered by the Empire, and the Emperor was intrigued by the prophetic abilities of the native species. Therefore, he instigated an [[Imperial Attack on Voss|attack]] on the planet by Imperial forces while his Hand kidnapped a [[Gender/Legends|male]] Voss [[Voss Mystics|Mystic]] from the surface.<ref name="Request An Audience" />

The Emperor would experiment with the Voss' powers over the next few years, using the abilities of his host<ref name="The Voice of Darknessnote">{{TORcite|type=class|Sith Warrior|The Voice of Darkness|Voss}} explains that the Emperor's essence can only change bodies when his current host dies, meaning that the Voice must have died or been killed.</ref> and those of a captive Revan<ref name="Maelstrom">{{TORcite|type=flashpoint|Maelstrom Prison}}</ref> to gaze into the future as he made preparations to repeat on a galactic scale the ritual that had given him immortality.<ref name="An Unthinkable Alliance">{{TORcite|type=class|Jedi Knight|An Unthinkable Alliance|the Emperor's Fortress}}</ref> However, Dark Councilor [[Darth Baras]] had been manipulating the Emperor throughout that period, feeding him information on the mysterious dark side entity known as [[Sel-Makor]] that resided in the Sith complex called the [[Dark Heart]] on Voss.<ref name="The Voice of Darkness" /> Finally, in [[3640 BBY]],<ref name="Time" /> the Emperor decided to investigate Sel-Makor in the event that the entity could be useful to his ongoing plans.<ref name="The Voice of Darkness" />

===Plots foiled===
{{Quote|Once I ascend, all will be tranquil in this galaxy. It is my promise to you. Now, strike!''"<br />"''No! Forever bound! Sel-Makor takes this body! Such&hellip; power!|Sel-Makor prevents the Wrath from freeing the Emperor|<ref name="The Voice of Darkness" />}}
[[File:BigBadSithEmperor.png|thumb|left|200px|The Emperor's Voice during his battle with the Hero of Tython]]
However, when the Voice entered the Ancient Halls of the Dark Heart, the Emperor found that he could not leave&mdash;the Ancient Halls were a place that no Voss could ever exit, just as Baras had planned. Before the Emperor could reach out to his Hand and explain Baras' betrayal, Sel-Makor seized control of the Voice and began to battle the Emperor for control of both his host and the Sith's own powers in the Force.<ref name="The Voice of Darkness" /> With the true Voice out of the way, Baras began his [[Darth Baras's coup|attempt]] to proclaim himself the Voice, betraying his [[Empire's Wrath|apprentice]] in the process. However, acting on the fragments of instructions that the Emperor was able to send them during his struggle, the Hand appointed Baras' apprentice the newest [[Emperor's Wrath]] and unleashed the [[Sith Warrior]] upon Baras' allies. The Wrath eventually located the true Voice on Voss, and after defeating it in [[Battle in the Ancient Halls|battle]] when Sel-Makor seized control of the body, the Wrath was ordered to kill the Voss host in order to free the Emperor's essence. With the death of his host, the Emperor's essence was able to return to his Hand and acquire a [[Unidentified Human Emperor's Voice (Galactic War)|Human male]] as his new host.<ref name="Doomsday">{{TORcite|type=class|Jedi Knight|Doomsday|Dromund Kaas}}</ref>

This Voice would ultimately fall in battle with the Emperor's enemy, the [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] known as the [[Hero of Tython]], when the Jedi [[Dromund Kaas operation|confronted]] the Sith ruler in the depths of the [[Dark Temple]] on the Imperial capital [[Dromund Kaas/Legends|Dromund Kaas]]. Despite all of the Emperor's power, the Knight was still able to strike him down and kill the Voice, grievously wounding the Emperor's essence with the power of the [[Light side of the Force/Legends|light side]].<ref name="Doomsday" /> Forced from their host, the Emperor's energies were left without an anchor and fell into a deep slumber at the shock of the blow.<ref name="The Emperor's Absence">{{TORcite|type=message|The Emperor's Absence|Servant One of the Emperor's Hand}}</ref> The injury also affected his control over his Valkorion body; Valkorion's power faltered, causing the mental blocks he had placed within the mind of his daughter [[Vaylin]] to lapse.<ref name="Vaylin">{{TORcite|type=codex|exp=kotfe|Vaylin}}</ref>

The Emperor's incorporeal essence took shelter in the dark side energies of the [[Moon/Legends|moon]] [[Yavin 4/Legends|Yavin 4]], and when the Sith Empire turned on their former ruler upon discovering his plans to destroy the galaxy,<ref name="Temple of Sacrifice">{{TORcite|exp=shadow|type=general|The Enemy Within}}</ref> the position of Voice was abandoned entirely&mdash;now known as Vitiate, the former Emperor did not take a new host and instead [[Invasion of Ziost|ravaged]] the planet [[Ziost/Legends|Ziost]]<ref name="The End of It All" /> before consolidating himself entirely in the Valkorion host body. Shortly afterward, the [[Yavin Coalition]], a joint task force between the Empire and the Republic that aimed to stop Vitiate's plans, then found Valkorion, who was slain in the ensuing confrontation.<ref name="KOTFE-1">{{TORcite|exp=kotfe|chapter=1}}</ref> Vitiate was thus forced to bond himself to [[Alliance Commander|the Outlander]], leader of the Yavin Coalition, although he sought to ally with the Outlander and did not make his new host into a true Voice.<ref name="Chapter 6">{{TORcite|exp=kotfe|chapter=6}}</ref> However, the Outlander refused to work with Valkorion and, as [[Commander]] of the [[Eternal Alliance]], eventually [[Mission to Kira Carsen's ship|destroyed]] the Emperor's true body<ref name="Echoes">{{TORcite|exp=ons|type=flashpoint|Echoes of Oblivion}}</ref> in [[3626 BBY]].<ref name="Update 6.2">{{TOR_updates|6.2}}</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|Remember that all those who have direct access to the Emperor&mdash;the Emperor's Voice, the Emperor's Hand, the soldiers in the Imperial Guard&mdash;are under his spell.|Darth Nyriss mentions the Voice, almost half a decade before the position was created|<ref name="Revan" />}}
The Emperor's Voice was first mentioned in the [[2011]] novel ''[[The Old Republic: Revan]]'' by the Dark Councilor [[Darth Nyriss]].<ref name="Revan" /> However, the [[2012]] reference guide ''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic Encyclopedia]]'' directly contradicted this statement, as it established that the Emperor created his first Voice ''after'' Revan attacked the Emperor in 3950 BBY, meaning that the position did not exist<ref name="Encyclopedia" /> when Nyriss mentioned them to Lord Scourge in [[3954 BBY]].<ref name="Revan" />
